claims.statement: ClinVar provides synchronized weekly downloads and APIs, versions assertions, exposes conflicts, and does not adjudicate ordinary submitter disagreements.
ACMG has published professional points to consider for genomic result reevaluation and reanalysis.
A large 2015-2023 cohort found 94,453 of 2,051,736 observed variants, 4.60%, were reclassified.
ESHG describes recontacting as potentially desirable but shared, consent-aware, resource-constrained, and lacking settled cost-effectiveness evidence.
Franklin, QIAGEN, and Fabric already offer monitoring, interpretation, reanalysis, or case-workflow capabilities.
A storage-transfer registry can sit outside device scope, but patient-specific interpretation or reprioritization may become IVD software; genetic data also receives GDPR Article 9 protection.

contrary_evidence: ClinVar's weekly API makes public assertion change detection a commodity input.
Franklin Community already follows variants and cases for new evidence.
QIAGEN and Fabric have mature clinical interpretation and workflow products.
ESHG does not establish a universal recontact duty or proven budget; it emphasizes shared responsibility and sustainability.

economics.acquisition_route: Sell a data-minimized operational module through one genetics laboratory or LIMS design partner; direct clinical sales and integrations are unvalidated and incumbent-heavy.
economics.founder_net_worth_path: High-uncertainty path: 90 accounts at 80000 PLN annual revenue equals 7.2 million PLN ARR; 25% EBITDA at 4x and 75% founder ownership implies about 5.4 million PLN founder equity in years 8-10, excluding distributions and retained cash.
economics.founder_time: Four to five founder hours daily for product and integrations, with clinical genetics, privacy, and security judgment delegated to qualified advisers and customer professionals.
economics.gross_margin_basis: Inference: 60-75% during integration-heavy deployment, potentially 75-85% after reusable LIMS connectors; security and support costs are unmeasured.
economics.payback: Unknown. A 60000 PLN annual contract pays back within 12-24 months only if it avoids roughly 300 hours at 200 PLN per hour or equivalent risk; no buyer time study validates this.
economics.pricing: Unvalidated: 30000-70000 PLN annual registry fee plus 15000-40000 PLN implementation; avoid autonomous interpretation and per-case pricing until value is proven.
economics.retention_or_repeat: Historical case mappings, review decisions, consent state, and audit continuity recur with every public or customer-authored assertion update.

fingerprint.compounding_advantage: Customer-specific case mappings, adjudication logs, consent records, and recontact outcomes deepen workflow rules and switching cost
fingerprint.customer: Genetic laboratories and inherited-disease clinics with longitudinal historical cohorts
fingerprint.distribution_mechanism: LIMS integrations and genetics-laboratory design partnerships
fingerprint.offer_and_business_model: Clinician-controlled assertion-change registry and consent-aware audit queue sold as annual SaaS plus implementation
fingerprint.payer_and_paid_event: The laboratory or clinic pays to maintain monitored case mappings and document each authorized review
fingerprint.problem_trigger: A public or customer-authored variant assertion changes relative to a prior patient report

founder_fit: Genetics interest and data-engineering skills fit identifier normalization, versioning, and audit workflows.
Clinical interpretation and recontact decisions remain with qualified laboratory professionals, so the founder need not supply non-delegable medical authority.
A single customer-funded integration can be attempted part-time, but a broad clinical deployment cannot be bootstrapped casually.
risks: Identifier or transcript mismatches may create missed or noisy case alerts.
Patient-specific prioritization or interpretation may trigger IVDR obligations.
Genetic data processing requires strict contracts, security, access controls, and a lawful basis.
Incumbents may bundle the narrow registry feature into existing interpretation suites.
Clinics may lack budget because recontact responsibility and practice remain unsettled.

structure.control_point: A longitudinal case-to-assertion graph with immutable review, consent, and recontact audit history
structure.critical_dependency: Secure LIMS linkage, accurate variant normalization, recorded consent, and a validated non-interpretive intended-use boundary

thesis: Build a data-minimized, clinician-controlled registry that maps public and customer-authored assertion version changes to pseudonymous historical cases and produces an auditable review queue without interpreting or reprioritizing medical significance. The moat is customer workflow history, not free ClinVar data.
title: Variant Recall Registry
uncertainties: Laboratory willingness to buy a narrow module rather than use Franklin or an existing interpretation suite is unknown.
LIMS integration effort, false-alert tolerance, and labor savings are unmeasured.
National recontact duties, consent practices, and procurement budgets vary.
The non-device boundary requires intended-use review and may not survive requested prioritization features.
